bugs.description: get_next_available_options consistently returns the same 3 stale slots (9:00, 9:40, 10:20 on 2026-07-04) that are already taken by other bookings. check_availability correctly rejects them. On each turn the LangGraph checkpoint replays the full context, resetting slot_iso back to 9:00, which is then rejected again. This creates an unresolvable loop: the user cannot book any slot because offered slots are always stale and the tool offers no fresh alternatives beyond the stale cache.
bugs.evidence: Turn 8: check_availability rejected 09:00 (slot_no_longer_available). Turn 9: check_availability rejected 10:20 (slot_no_longer_available). Turn 10: check_availability rejected 09:00 and 10:20 again; update_booking rejected 11:00 with reoffer_slots because it was not in the get_next_available_options output.

bugs.description: Each turn the agent re-replays all update_booking calls from the beginning, including the initial ones with empty fields (audience=null, services=[corte de pelo] without resolved IDs). This inflates token usage and causes the slot_iso to be reset to the first-offered (stale) slot on every turn, contributing to the staleness loop.
bugs.evidence: Turn 8-10 tool_evidence all begin with update_booking({audience: null, pre_resolved_service_ids: null, ...}) before rebuilding context from checkpoint replay.
